headlines.title: 개도국에 ‘ 韓 AI기술 ’ 이식한다 … 정부, ODA 연계 해외진출 지원
headlines.summary: 구윤철, 대외경제장관 회의서 K-AI 패키지 발굴전략 등 논의 정부가 개발도상국에 인공지능(AI) 솔루션과 데이터센터, 신재생에너지 발전설비를 한꺼번에 지원하는 ‘K-AI 패키지’를 추진한다. 개도국의 성장을 지원하는 동시에 국내 AI·데이터센터·에너지 기업의 해외 진출 기회도 넓히겠다는 구상이다.

headlines.title: 구윤철 “ 하반기 경제 현안 산적 … 국민 체감 변화에 역량 집중 ”
headlines.summary: 구윤철 경제부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관은 “하반기에도 경제 현안과 정책 과제가 산적한 상황”이라며 “국민이 체감할 수 있는 변화를 만들어 내는 데 역량을 집중해달라”고 주요 간부들에게 당부했습니다. 구 부총리는 오늘(20일) 정부세종청사에서 확대간부회의를 열고 이같이 말했습니다.

headlines.title: 구윤철 " 정책 과제 국민 체감 성과로 이어지도록 후속 조치 만전 "
headlines.summary: 핵심요약 재정경제부 확대간부회의 개최 구윤철 부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관이 20일 정부세종청사에서 열린 대외경제장관회의에서 모두발언을 하고 있다. 연합뉴스 구윤철 부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관이 하반기 경제정책 방향과 주요 과제들이 국민이 체감할 수 있는 가시적 성과로 이어질 수 있도록 후속 조치를 차질 없이 추진할 것을 당부했다.

headlines.title: 법인 실소유자 등록제 ‘ 실질과세 ’ 추진
headlines.summary: 정부, 등기처럼 명부화 구상 역외탈세 대응 등 제도 개편 정부가 법인·신탁 등에 대한 실질 소유자를 법원 등기처럼 명부화해 과세 대상을 분명히 하는 제도 마련에 착수했다. 해외 페이퍼컴퍼니 설립, 해외자산 은닉 등 역외탈세 시도에 대응하기 위해 관련 제도를 도입한 국가가 늘자 국내 실정에 맞는 제도 도입 가능성을 살펴보겠다는 것이다.

headlines.title: 초고가 1주택 정조준 …‘ 40억 기준 ’ 과세표준 재설정 가능성
headlines.summary: ■ 이달말 세제개편안 이목 김용범 실장, 보유세 강화 시사 오늘부터는 비아파트 공급 지원 서울 서초구 아파트 전경. 독자제공 김용범 청와대 정책실장이 실거주 1주택자라도 ‘초고가 주택’에 대해서는 보유세 부담을 늘리는 방안을 검토 중임을 시사하면서 이달 말 발표될 세제개편안 내용에 시선이 집중되고 있다.

headlines.title: 오피스텔·도생 공급 속도 … 토지비 지원 최대 80 %
headlines.summary: 오늘 비아파트 주택공급대책 시행 HUG, 도심주택특약보증 개편 올해 접수 사업 모두 소급 적용 전체 동 아닌 부분 매입 허용 공사비 先 착공-後 검증 시행 올해 비아파트 신축매입임대주택을 공급하기로 한 사업자는 정부의 토지확보 지원금을 최대 80%까지 지원받을 수 있게 됐다.

headlines.title: “ 서울 ‘ 상위 1% 아파트 ’ 진입가격 46억5000만원 ”
headlines.summary: 직방, 상반기 지역별 상위 1% 아파트 분석 경기 18.5억·대구 15.8억, 지역차 최대 9배 ‘상위 1%’ 서울 아파트를 사려면 최소 46억5000만원 가량이 있어야 하는 것으로 나타났다. 정부가 초고가 주택에 대해 차등적으로 보유 부담을 강화하기로 하면서 기준선이 어느선으로 정해질지 관심이 모아지고 있다.

headlines.title: ‘영끌·빚투족’ 비상… 기준금리 인상 시 주담대·신용대출 이자 부담 ...
headlines.summary: 한은, 기준금리 3~4회 인상 전망…취약차주·변동금리 차주 부담 커질 듯 이종욱 “청년·실수요층 이자 폭탄 우려…정부, 가계부채 리스크 점검해야” 서울 한 은행에 붙은 대출 안내문 모습. 연합뉴스 한국은행이 기준금리 인상 가능성을 열어둔 가운데, 이른바 ‘영끌’과 ‘빚투’ 차주들의 이자 부담이 크게 늘어날 수 있다는 분석이 나왔다.

headlines.title: [ 원화 국제화, 30년 금기 깨다]①비로소 국경 넘는다… 원화 위상, 경제 ...

headlines.summary: 9월부터 역외 원화 결제 시스템 시범 운영 해외서 원화 계좌 개설·외국인 간 송금 가능 외국인 원화 대출·증권 발행 신고 규제도 푼다 금리 인하·보험 확대…결제 수요에 인센티브도 원화 장기 보유·투자 매력 높이는 것이 관건 “한국 경제 체급에 걸맞은 금융시장 경쟁력 갖춰야” 편집자주 원화가 큰 변화의 길목에 섰다.

headlines.summary: 2000억 확보, 法 즉시항고 수용가능 회생절차 재개땐 9월 4일까지 연장 협력사 이탈에 잔존사업 M&A 불투명 파산 수순을 밟던 홈플러스가 회생에 필요한 최소 자금인 2000억원 규모의 긴급 자금을 확보하며 회생의 불씨를 살렸다. 다만 영업 정상화나 인수·합병(M&A)까지는 아직 넘어야 할 산이 많다.

key_headlines.title: Household Debt Crisis Looms as Base Rate Hikes Expected
key_headlines.summary: The Bank of Korea is expected to raise the base rate 3-4 times, which will significantly increase interest burdens for vulnerable borrowers and variable-rate mortgage holders, particularly young people and first-time homebuyers.

key_headlines.title: Government Prepares Major Real Estate and Tax Reform Announcements
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yun-chul announced preparations for a large-scale real estate discussion conference and tax reform package by end of month to deliver tangible economic benefits to citizens.

key_headlines.title: Ultra-Luxury Housing Tax Overhaul Under Review at 4 Billion Won Threshold
key_headlines.summary: The government is considering resetting the taxable standard for ultra-high-priced single-family homes at around 4 billion won, with strengthened holding taxes for luxury properties regardless of primary residence status.

key_headlines.title: Seoul's Top 1% Apartment Entry Price Reaches 46.5 Billion Won
key_headlines.summary: Real estate platform Zigbang reported that purchasing a top 1% apartment in Seoul requires a minimum of 46.5 billion won, highlighting massive regional disparities with entry prices ranging up to 9 times lower in other regions.

key_headlines.title: Government Launches K-AI Package for Developing Nations
key_headlines.summary: The government is promoting a 'K-AI Package' combining AI solutions, data centers, and renewable energy equipment for developing countries, creating overseas expansion opportunities for domestic tech and energy companies.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea faces mounting household debt pressures as the Bank of Korea signals potential base rate increases of 3-4 times in the coming period. Young people and variable-rate borrowers face escalating interest payment burdens, raising concerns about household financial vulnerability. Meanwhile, the government is preparing comprehensive real estate and tax reform packages to be announced by month-end, aiming to deliver visible economic improvements to citizens. Luxury property taxation is also undergoing significant revision, with discussions centering on a 4 billion won threshold for enhanced holding taxes. These policy moves reflect the government's effort to address mounting economic inequality and housing affordability concerns.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's economy continues on a positive trajectory with Q2 2026 real GDP growth of 0.3% quarter-over-quarter, supported by semiconductor boom and IT investments. The country's per capita GDP is projected to reach nearly 40,000 dollars this year, with an expected breakthrough above 40,000 dollars next year, marking the largest five-year increase since 2021. The government projects nominal GDP growth of 12.3% for the year, the highest level in 30 years since 1996, driven by semiconductor export surge. However, employment growth has not kept pace with economic gains, as college graduates face limited job opportunities despite overall economic recovery. The government plans to redirect excess tax revenues to youth investment and future-oriented infrastructure to address AI-driven employment disruption.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korean stock markets experienced significant volatility with KOSPI declining approximately 25% from June highs, partly attributed to leverage ETF amplification effects. Single-stock leverage ETFs for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, launched in May, have become increasingly controversial as they magnify price swings in semiconductor stocks amid recent weakness. The won-dollar exchange rate fluctuated between 1,470 and 1,480 won, influenced by SK Hynix's Nasdaq listing effects and Middle East geopolitical tensions. Market participants anticipate continued volatility ahead of the Federal Reserve's late-July policy meeting and Korea's Q2 GDP announcement. Financial institutions are introducing new products like target-conversion funds with 6% return objectives to navigate uncertain market conditions.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's semiconductor exports surged 229% year-over-year, with Pyeongtaek Customs recording record high exports and a decade-high trade surplus of 14.61 billion dollars. The semiconductor industry continues to drive economic growth, supported by strong AI server demand and data center expansion globally. Lithium battery storage safety concerns emerged at a Coupang logistics center in Incheon, containing the equivalent of 20 electric vehicles' worth of batteries, highlighting risks in rapidly expanding e-commerce infrastructure. Korea is preparing to invest in first major U.S. projects focusing on energy, shipbuilding, and data centers, with the Industry Minister scheduled to visit the U.S. for final negotiations on July 23rd.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's real estate market faces intensifying policy debates between the central government and city administration regarding redevelopment and reconstruction as housing supply solutions. Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon strongly criticized the current government's regulatory approach, arguing that redevelopment and reconstruction are the 'master key' for urban housing supply, contradicting policy officials' assessments of limited short-term benefits. Jeonse (lease deposit) listings have declined sharply, particularly in affordable neighborhoods, with some districts experiencing 82% year-over-year decreases, indicating market contraction in lower-priced areas. The government continues prioritizing strict regulations and financial measures for real estate stability, while local authorities push for accelerated development and reduced restrictions. Tension remains high over whether to implement differentiated taxation on ultra-luxury properties above 4 billion won.
sections.International Economy: Global tariff policies remain in flux with a 24-day tariff period deadline approaching and country-specific tariff announcements pending, with Korea positioned to defend its current 15% tariff rate. The U.S. manufacturing sector's share of GDP has continued declining, falling from 10.7% in Q1 2017 to 9.4% in Q1 2026, reflecting structural economic changes despite Trump administration's protectionist policies. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Wash has maintained a cautious stance with limited public communication, causing market uncertainty about future monetary policy direction ahead of the late-July FOMC meeting. Trade tensions persist between the U.S. and other nations, including Brazil receiving 25% tariffs on tech-related disputes, setting precedent for broader trade conflicts. International markets remain sensitive to geopolitical risks, particularly Middle East tensions, which are supporting oil prices and influencing currency movements.
sections.AI & Economy: AI semiconductor demand remains robust with multiple Korean companies posting strong earnings growth in the first half of 2026, driven by data center expansion and server development. Padu, a data center semiconductor company, recorded 73.15 billion won in Q2 revenue and 16.26 billion won operating profit, expecting stronger second-half performance from increased storage controller demand. Gaon Cable achieved record first-half operating profit of 64 billion won, benefiting from U.S. power infrastructure investments and AI-related expansion requirements. TSMC confirmed strong multi-year structural demand for AI semiconductors and committed to continued capital investments in U.S. production facilities. The government is actively promoting AI talent development initiatives, with Seoul's Youth Employment Officer School focusing on cultivating AI professionals to meet future industry needs.
sections.Others: The government faces structural challenges in coordinating youth employment policy, with over 300 youth-focused policies implemented but lacking a unified control tower for cohesive implementation. Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yun-chul, marking his second year in office, emphasized the need to deliver tangible economic improvements to citizens while addressing multiple challenges including tariff negotiations, Middle East conflicts, and youth employment slowdown. Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon is actively promoting AI talent development through the Youth Employment Officer School and other initiatives to prepare young people for future industry demands. Government agencies are implementing various safety and industrial initiatives, including Koryoung Zinc's Onsan Smeltery receiving excellence awards for safety education program development. The Trump administration continues emphasizing economic pressure through expanded sanctions against Russia and Iran, signaling ongoing trade and geopolitical tensions that affect Korean economic interests.
